message.content:
Based on my search, I can provide you with comprehensive information about methane bonding.

## Methane Bond Structure

**Molecular Formula:** CH₄

### Type of Bonding
Methane consists of **four covalent bonds** between one central carbon atom and four hydrogen atoms. These are specifically **sigma (σ) bonds** formed through the sharing of electron pairs between atoms.

### Bond Formation Details
- **Carbon** has 4 valence electrons and needs 4 more to complete its octet
- **Each hydrogen** has 1 valence electron and needs 1 more to complete its duet
- Carbon shares one electron with each of the four hydrogen atoms, forming four single covalent bonds
- Each C-H bond consists of a shared pair of electrons

### Hybridization and Geometry
- The carbon atom in methane undergoes **sp³ hybridization**
- One s orbital and three p orbitals of carbon mix to form four equivalent **sp³ hybrid orbitals**
- These four sp³ orbitals then form sigma bonds with the 1s orbitals of four hydrogen atoms
- The resulting molecular geometry is **tetrahedral**

### Structural Characteristics
| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| H-C-H bond angle | 109.5° |
| C-H bond length | 108.70 pm (approximately 1.09 Å) |
| Molecular shape | Tetrahedral |

### Key Properties Due to Its Bonding
- **Nonpolar molecule:** The C-H bonds are only slightly polar, and due to the symmetrical tetrahedral arrangement, any bond dipoles cancel out
- **Poor electrical conductor:** No charged particles (ions) are present since electrons are shared, not transferred
- **Low melting and boiling points:** Weak intermolecular forces (London dispersion forces) between nonpolar methane molecules
- **Very low boiling point:** -162°C

### Three-Dimensional Representation
When drawing methane's structure in 2D:
- Two C-H bonds are shown as straight lines in the plane of the paper
- One bond is shown as a **solid wedge** (coming out toward the viewer)
- One bond is shown as a **dashed line** (going behind the plane)

This tetrahedral structure maximizes the distance between the four bonding electron pairs, minimizing electron-electron repulsion according to VSEPR theory, which explains why methane adopts this geometry rather than a square planar arrangement.

Sources:
1. https://www.chemtube3d.com/vseprshapech4/
2. https://www.askiitians.com/forums/11-grade-chemistry-others/explain-the-bonding-in-methane-molecules-using-ele-25_495730.htm
3. https://eresources.blog/methane-bond-line-structure-explained
4. https://scholarworks.alaska.edu/bitstream/handle/11122/14963/Mahmuda_S_2023.pdf?sequence=1&isAllowed=y
5. https://cdn.savemyexams.com/pdfs/-d6514aiPC3bgI.pdf
6. https://guao.org/sites/default/files/biblioteca/153281083-CK-12-Chemistry-Concepts-Intermediate-Julio-2013.pdf
7. https://www.nygh.sg/lower_secondary_science/sec_one_science/sec_one_chemistry/chemical_bonding_lower_sec.pdf
